paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithms for Differential Equations in Finance and Physics

experiments.description: Approximate Grover-Rudolph amplitude loading of a normal distribution, including clustering of rotation angles and robustness analysis under realistic IBM Jakarta noise.

algorithm.variant: Grover-Rudolph via approximated unitary map with angle clustering
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Choose clustering level ko such that target infidelity epsilon is met; numerical examples use epsilon = 0.05 and also analyze fidelity maxima over ko.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Encode a discretized positive density function into amplitudes of an n-qubit state; for the normal distribution the target state is the discretized normal density on [0,1] (after standardization in the paper's notation).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |f>_n approximating the discretized density function f with fidelity at least 1 - epsilon.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Angle clustering for blocks satisfying the smoothness bound; no penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: Normal distribution loading example used to benchmark the approximate Grover-Rudolph protocol.

dataset_specification.description: Mean mu = 0.5; variance sigma varied over {1.0, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3}; n = 8 qubits; clustering starts at different ko values.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize the density on an n-qubit grid; compute rotation angles from conditional probabilities; cluster angles in blocks where the second derivative of log f is bounded.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation of fidelity and two-qubit gate reduction; Table 3.1 and Fig. 3.5 report fidelities for different sigma and ko values.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Native gate set CNOT, Id, Rz(theta), X, S
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute Grover-Rudolph angles from the target density; determine clustering threshold ko from the smoothness bound.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity and L2-norm error against the exact discretized state.

results.unit: x faster than ideal circuit-model quantum computer

speedup_claims.factor: exponential spatial compression / O(log N) state preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: for loading discretized functions into amplitudes; assuming efficient angle computation and smoothness conditions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that the exact Grover-Rudolph unitary-map implementation has exponential gate cost, while the approximated clustered version reduces two-qubit gates at the expense of controllable infidelity.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming native implementation of arbitrary single-qubit rotations and 2-qubit unitaries, gate time 25 ns, and analog energy scale H0B(1)J = 1 rad/ns
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a physical runtime estimate excluding state preparation, device programming, and readout times; also assumes no compilation overhead into a finite universal gate set.

experiments.description: Variational Grover-Rudolph extension for loading non-smooth functions, demonstrated on a sine function and on the Black-Scholes payoff distribution.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Stop when the difference between the cost function of two consecutive steps is below the tolerance, or when the training loop stopping criteria is met.
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialized with Grover-Rudolph angles; compared against random uniform initialization in [0, pi].

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Encode target function values into amplitudes of an n-qubit state; cluster angles except near zeros and singular points.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize mean squared error between target discretized amplitudes and circuit-generated amplitudes.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Cluster angles corresponding to non-special points; keep explicit parameters near zeros/singularities.

problem_instance.description: Two benchmark functions: normalized sine function on [0, pi] and Black-Scholes backward PDE initial payoff distribution.

dataset_specification.description: Sine function on [0, pi]; Black-Scholes distribution with K = 45 and c = 3; n = 5 qubits for the main Black-Scholes example and n = 12, 15, 16, 17, 18 for scalability/training comparisons.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize the target function on the qubit grid; for Black-Scholes, use the payoff function as the initial state for later Hamiltonian simulation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Report fidelities for different p(k) values and compare Grover-Rudolph initialization versus random initialization; Table 3.4 reports average steps and fidelities over 40 random initializations.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute target amplitudes and initialize parameters from Grover-Rudolph angles.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity, number of optimization steps, and compare against random initializations.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the variational Grover-Rudolph extension on the tested sine and Black-Scholes examples
speedup_claims.caveats: The improvement is empirical and problem-dependent; the paper reports fewer optimization steps and slightly better fidelities when initialized with Grover-Rudolph angles.

speedup_claims.conditions: Grover-Rudolph initialization used to seed gradient descent for loading non-smooth functions
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports improved training behavior and slightly improved final fidelity, but no explicit speedup factor or runtime comparison is given in the extracted text.

experiments.description: Exact and approximate loading of the linear function using the discrete Hadamard-Walsh transform, including noisy simulations and comparison with MPS loading.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Load the linear function into amplitudes via its Hadamard-Walsh series; exact loading uses all terms, approximate loading truncates to the largest ko terms.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare the discretized linear function state |dL>_n or its approximation with controlled fidelity and reduced gate count.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation of Hadamard-Walsh coefficients; no penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: Linear function loading benchmark on n = 6 qubits, with noisy and ideal comparisons.

dataset_specification.description: Linear function on [0,1]; exact and approximate loading compared for n = 6 and ko = 3; MPS X = 1 included as a baseline comparison.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute DHWT coefficients, truncate to ko terms, renormalize amplitudes, and compare to exact state.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare fidelity and L2 norm in ideal and noisy simulations; Fig. 3.17 reports the trade-off versus ko.

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Native gate set CNOT, Id, Rz(theta), X, S
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute DHWT coefficients and truncation index ko; compare against exact linear function and MPS X = 1.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity and L2 norm; compare ideal versus noisy results.

speedup_claims.factor: O(n) gate complexity for exact linear loading; O(ko) for truncated loading
speedup_claims.conditions: for the linear function encoded via DHWT; approximate truncation with ko=3 on n=6 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: The approximate method introduces controllable truncation error; noisy simulations use IBM Jakarta calibration parameters.

speedup_claims.conditions: Comparison of exact/approximate DHWT loading against MPS with bond dimension 1
speedup_claims.caveats: The excerpt reports comparable fidelities and noisy-vs-ideal comparisons, but no explicit speedup factor.

experiments.description: Polynomial loading via block encoding and QSVT, using the linear-function loader as a subroutine and comparing DHWT+QSVT against MPS-based loading.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: First load the linear function into amplitudes on ko qubits, then block-encode those amplitudes and apply QSVT to transform them into polynomial amplitudes; remaining qubits are padded to obtain an n-qubit approximation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Encode a target polynomial P(x) into amplitudes of a quantum state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Amplitude amplification after QSVT; optional importance sampling when P(0) <= 0 is satisfied.

problem_instance.description: Polynomial function encoding benchmark on n = 6 qubits, comparing DHWT+QSVT, linear MPS+QSVT, and direct polynomial MPS methods.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Load the linear function exactly or approximately, block-encode amplitudes, apply QSVT polynomial transformation, then pad remaining qubits.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare L2 norm error and fidelity across methods; Table 3.7 and Table 3.9 report fidelities for different polynomial degrees.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute block encoding of the linear function, QSVT angles, and polynomial rescaling; compare against direct polynomial MPS loading.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity and L2 norm; tabulate performance versus polynomial degree and loading method.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial transformation with O(d ko) circuit depth
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming an efficient block encoding of the linear function and QSVT polynomial transformation
speedup_claims.caveats: The overall cost depends on the filling ratio F and on the cost of the linear-function loader; the paper notes that some transformations may still be expensive.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: linear MPS + QSVT / direct polynomial MPS
speedup_claims.conditions: Polynomial encoding benchmark on n = 6 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: The excerpt indicates a comparison of methods and fidelity tables, but no explicit runtime or asymptotic speedup claim is stated in the provided text.

experiments.description: Black-Scholes option pricing simulation via Hamiltonian simulation with unitary dilation and postselection, including discretization and success-probability analysis.

algorithm.variant: Hamiltonian simulation of non-Hermitian Black-Scholes dynamics with unitary dilation
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state is the European put payoff after shifting and duplication to enforce periodic boundary conditions.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Encode the discretized payoff function into amplitudes of the position register; use one ancilla qubit for unitary dilation of the non-Hermitian propagator.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Simulate the Black-Scholes backward PDE and recover option prices from the evolved quantum state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Shift and duplicate the initial condition to impose periodic boundary conditions; postselect ancilla in |0_E>.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_BS = i((sigma^2/2 - r)p^2 - r p + i r I) in the paper's notation after change of variables and momentum operator definition.

problem_instance.description: European put option pricing under the Black-Scholes model.

dataset_specification.description: Parameters used in the figures: Smax = 150, K = 50, sigma = 0.2, r = 0.04, T = 1 year; discretization with n = 8 qubits for the main simulation and n = 9 when counting the duplicated-condition register in the figure caption.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Change variables S = exp(x); shift the payoff support to a symmetric interval; duplicate the initial condition by reflection to mitigate periodic boundary artifacts; discretize position and momentum with finite differences and QFT.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare numerical solution against analytical solution; report discretization error per point and postselection success probability as a function of maturity and interest rate.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the Black-Scholes PDE, build position and momentum operators, shift and duplicate the payoff, and construct the unitary dilation embedding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla and, upon success, recover option prices from the main register; compute success probability and compare to analytical solution.

speedup_claims.factor: optimal sparse Hamiltonian simulation / logarithmic resource scaling in grid size
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical PDE simulation / classical option pricing discretization
speedup_claims.conditions: for the Black-Scholes PDE after mapping to a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and using QFT-based diagonalization plus unitary dilation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report a direct wall-clock speedup; it argues complexity equivalence to non-Hermitian Hamiltonian simulation and notes that postselection success probability remains above 0.6 in the tested parameter range.

speedup_claims.conditions: Black-Scholes Hamiltonian simulation with unitary dilation and postselection
speedup_claims.caveats: The excerpt describes the method and parameters but does not provide a direct classical runtime or error baseline in the provided text.
